To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
catechol, p‐methyl‐catechol and hydroquinone are tumor‐promoting in the pyloric region of rat stomach, but catechol is the most potent, followed by p‐methyl­catechol and then hydroquinone.

the possible tumor promoting and tumor initiating activities of catechols in rat stomach are several times higher that those of p‐methyIcatechol and about 10 times higher that those or methylhydroquinone.

the possible tumor-promoting and tumor-initiating activities of catechols in the pyloric gland mucosa of rat stomach are dependent upon their structure, i.e. the number and position of methyl groups in catechols.
In summary, our research is concerned with

a study of the possible tumor‐initiating and tumor‐promoting activity of p‐methylene catechol and methyl hydroquinone, two compounds which are formed in rat stomach after oral administration of catechols.
the possible tumor‐initiating and promoting activities of p‐methy1catechol and methy1hydroquinone in rat pyloric mucosa.
a new hypothesis that the possible tumor initiation and promotion of catechol in the stomach of rats may be due to its metabolism to the corresponding p‐methylated compounds.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
catechol is a tumor promoter in rat stomach.
catechol has tumor‐initiating and tumor‐promoting potential, but the tumor‐initiating potential of p‐mec and methylhydroquinon is low or nil.
p‐methyl catechol and methyl‐hydroquinone have possible tumor‐initiating activity, but only p‐methyl‐catechol has possible tumor‐promoter activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
catechol is a strong tumor promoter and a weak initiator, p‐methyl catechol is only a strong tumor promoter, and methylhydroquinon is a weak tumor promoter and a possible initiator.

the possible tumor initiation and promotion by p‐methyl catechol and methyl hydroquinone are less than those of catechol, and that catechol may be a tumor‐initiating and promoting agent in rat stomach.
